author: Ed Nice
title: Financial Struggles In Buffalo: What's The Budget Deficit? - NewsBreak
text:
By Ed Nice ,
8 hours ago
New York’s second-largest city has been dealing with some pretty serious financial issues over the last couple of years. It was just over a year ago when city officials used a large chunk of the federal COVID-19 stimulus funds to plug some holes in the city’s bank account. Now with those funds gone, there are more issues that need to be solved.
Not only is Buffalo dealing with a reduction in its credit score , but it has raised fees in all sorts of places to try to make up the shortfall.
While there are tons of proposals to increase revenue, until those materialize, the city still has to find millions of dollars in funds in order to be able to pay all of its bills this year. Unfortunately, there is some major disagreement on how much money is needed to pay those bills.
Government Officials Can’t Agree On How Much Buffalo’s Budget Deficit Is Over the months, there has been a major dispute between the Mayor’s office, the Buffalo Common Council, and the City Comptroller about the city’s budget and exactly how short the government will be when the end of the fiscal year comes in June. While there is no dispute that there is a deficit, the is a big dispute on how big the deficit is.
Now, thanks to a quarterly financial report that was issued by the Comptroller this week , the debate on the deficit figures is back in the news again, and the potential dollar amount is staggering.
READ MORE: Does Buffalo Need A Public Advocate Like In New York City?
According to the First Quarter Gap Report issued by City Comptroller Barbara Miller-Williams, the city’s projected deficit is at least $42.8 million and could be as much as $80.3 million for this year alone.
Several Buffalo Common Council Members, who reviewed the Gap Report during the city’s first council meeting of the year, took issue with the figures, with South District Council Member Scanlon calling it wildly irresponsible to put these numbers out for the public .
Ed Nice Jackson Current Buffalo Mayor Sean Ryan has said that New York State may be willing to help the city shore up its finances in the short term, and Governor Kathy Hochul said that this is something that is on the table. We’re going to have to wait and see if things get better or worse in Buffalo.
Highlights from 2024-25 City of Buffalo Budget The 2024-25 City of Buffalo budget took effect on July 1, 2024. The overall value of the budget is pegged at $1,897,022,771 Gallery Credit: Ed Nice Photo by CDC on Unsplash $1,297,869,282 - Buffalo Board of Education The city budget's most significant part goes to Buffalo Public Schools, which, according to Buffalo Business First , spends just under $26,000 per student. Andrew Harnik / Getty Images $109,169,773 - Buffalo Police Department A significant expense for the city is for police services. The Buffalo Police Department is also planning to purchase new cars for officers and already has purchased new guns for them, Photo by Connor Betts on Unsplash $72,747,784 - Buffalo Fire Department Many municipalities in Western New York have to rely on volunteer fire departments; that is not the case in Buffalo, which has one of the best-trained fire departments in the state. Joe Raedle / Getty Images $187,897,577 - Fringe Benefits for City Employees With such a large workforce, the city has to provide all sorts of additional services for them. Expenses such as retirement payments, health and life insurance, workers' compensation, and other expenses add up. Fatih Aktas / Anadolu Agency via Getty Images $42,413,728 - Debt Service Payments The City of Buffalo pays for some expenses using debt. Whether it's bonds or loans, the city doesn't always use its own cash to fund projects. These funds represent the loan payments and interest the city needs to pay on that debt.
